safety_note: This package records source facts and review questions only. Janani must not prescribe, start, stop, increase, decrease, inject or replace iron, folic acid, calcium or vitamin D based on this draft. Treating-clinician instructions outrank every candidate below.

source_facts: Current NHM AMB programme material advises 400 mcg folic acid daily in the pre-conception period and up to the first trimester.
review_questions: Should Janani surface this only as national-programme education unless the user's clinician has already entered/prescribed a regimen?
How should high-risk folic-acid indications be excluded from generic consumer messaging?

source_facts: Current NHM AMB programme material lists one IFA tablet daily from the fourth month/second trimester, minimum 180 days in pregnancy and 180 days postpartum.
The listed tablet contains 60 mg elemental iron and 500 mcg folic acid.
review_questions: Should Janani ever show the programme dose proactively, or only explain/remind a regimen already entered by the mother/clinician?
Confirm exact gestational start wording for consumer use: fourth month versus second trimester.

source_facts: The December 2025 ICMR ANC STW lists IFA once daily if Hb >11 g% and twice daily if Hb <11 g% during the second-trimester workflow.
The current NHM programme page provides prophylactic IFA facts but delegates anaemia treatment protocols to operational guidance.
candidates.block_reason: Full 2026 AMB treatment-protocol extraction and clinician reconciliation are required before interpreting the ICMR Hb-dependent dosing statement for consumer software.

source_facts: The ICMR ANC STW states referral to a higher centre if there is no rise in Hb after four weeks of oral tablets.
candidates.block_reason: Janani does not yet have a validated typed longitudinal haemoglobin-treatment-response rule that can distinguish adherence, timing, units and clinical context.

source_facts: The ICMR ANC STW contains parenteral-iron language for non-compliance or Hb <9 g% and referral language for Hb <7 g%.
The same STW lists Hb <7 g% among high-risk pregnancy criteria.
candidates.block_reason: Janani must never infer or recommend parenteral iron. Any Hb-based escalation requires typed confirmed laboratory observations, unit validation, date/provenance checks and clinician-approved urgency wording.

source_facts: The national calcium guideline specifies two 500 mg elemental-calcium doses per day from 14 weeks, each with 250 IU vitamin D3 and taken with meals.
The December 2025 ICMR ANC STW independently lists calcium carbonate 500 mg with vitamin D 250 units twice daily with meals.
review_questions: Confirm whether Janani should display formulation/dose only when explaining an existing prescription rather than initiating supplementation.
Confirm whether current national programme implementation still uses the 2014 vitamin-D formulation universally.

source_facts: The national calcium guideline states calcium and IFA should not be taken together.
The December 2025 ICMR ANC STW also states calcium carbonate and IFA should not be given together.
review_questions: Approve consumer-safe wording that says not to take them together without inventing an exact separation interval not stated consistently across current sources.
Confirm reminder scheduling behavior when a clinician has entered both medicines at the same time.

source_facts: The 2014 national calcium guideline specifies continuation through six months postpartum.
The 2025 one-page ICMR ANC STW confirms pregnancy calcium use but does not provide an equivalent postpartum duration statement.
The national calcium guideline advises calcium with meals and against taking both calcium tablets together.
The ICMR ANC STW also lists calcium twice daily with meals.

package_level_blocks: Full item-level extraction of the 2026 AMB operational guideline before anaemia treatment rules are considered.
Qualified obstetric/maternal-health clinician review of all Hb thresholds, dose statements and escalation wording.
Typed laboratory-observation model for Hb with unit/date/provenance validation before Hb can drive deterministic safety decisions.
Medication-timing policy that never changes a clinician-entered prescription without explicit clinician/user action.
Reviewed English consumer wording, followed by separate Telugu/Hindi clinical-language review.
